newsitem.title: USA: America Online sees rise in hourly use.
newsitem.headline: America Online sees rise in hourly use.

text.p: America Online Inc. said Monday it expected the number of hours each member uses the electronic subscription service every month to rise in fiscal 1997 from fiscal 1996.
In a 10-K filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the company cited the availability of its "Value Plan," which will allow subscribers to spend more time online at a lower cost.
Overall monthly online service revenue per AOL user in fiscal 1997 is expected to be comparable to fiscal 1996, the company said.
America Online unveiled the "Value Plan" pricing plan earlier this year to improve retention among its heavier users.
The new pricing plan, which became effective July 1, includes 20 hours of service for $19.95 per month, with a $2.95 hourly fee for usage exceeding 20 hours per month.

America Online said the new plan will boost the number of hours used relative to revenues. The average number of hours used per member per month in fiscal 1996 measured 6.86, up from 5.97 recorded for fiscal 1995, the company said.
For fiscal 1996, online service revenues nearly tripled to $991 million from $344 million in fiscal 1995, primarily due to a 93 percent increase in the number of subscribers, the filing said.
The company reported a subscriber base of 6.2 million members as of June 30, more than double the number from the end of fiscal 1995, it said.
